clue.text: Try to shag a party …

parts.note: to have someone is slang for to have sex with them
taken as written
a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: An invitation to try seducing a whole party, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash is an informal idiom for making an attempt at something.

clue.text: Bush seized: at the complete mercy of another

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: bush is slang for pubic hair, so someone grabbed by those hairs

definitions.text: at the complete mercy of another
definitions.meaning: second meaning: utterly in someone else's power, the figurative sense of the idiom

explanation.surface: A newly elected American president is captured and helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three lights: the second part is the light at 22 and the rest is at 4. Curlies are pubic hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Held by the short and curlies is a crude British idiom for being completely in someone's power.

clue.text: Crafty explorers skiving off

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters of skiving are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cunning adventurers are bunking off work.
explanation.walkthrough: Crafty looks like cunning; it means using sea craft, boats. Skiving is British slang for shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were Norse seafarers who explored and raided across Europe and the North Atlantic by ship.

clue.text: Make a bad egg churchman piss about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the beer goes round the churchman

parts.note: piss is British slang for weak beer, so ale
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree

explanation.surface: A clergyman who drinks heavily turns into a disgraceful character.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad egg looks like a scoundrel; here it is literally a rotten egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle an egg is to make it rotten, so it no longer hatches or is edible.

clue.text: See 1
Hill-billy's hard penis lacking depth

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for depth is dropped from the word for penis

parts.note: dick is slang for penis

explanation.surface: A backwoodsman's erection, but without much length to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Hill-billy stands for 'is'. H is the pencil-grade mark for hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hick is an unsophisticated country person, the same as a hillbilly.

clue.text: … girl who's slim, sly, promiscuous boozer

indicators.note: promiscuous suggests mixing indiscriminately, so the letters of sly are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a boozer is a pub, abbreviated PH for public house

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues the previous clue: the party features a slim, sly, promiscuous drinking girl.
explanation.walkthrough: PH (public house) is the map abbreviation for a pub, and boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a slender, graceful young woman, named after the airy spirits of folklore.

clue.text: Labour's bound to create a means of exploiting workers

parts.note: sweat is hard toil or labour
the possessive ending gives the letter S
to bound is to leap, to hop

explanation.surface: The Labour party is sure to set up a way of exploiting the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital looks like the political party; it is plain hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory where workers are paid little for long hours in poor conditions.

clue.text: Piss-artist stuck in terrible hole in African enclave

indicators.note: stuck in places the drunk inside the jumbled hole
terrible signals that hole is in a mess, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a piss-artist is British slang for a drunkard, a sot

explanation.surface: A drunk is trapped in an awful pit somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, making it an enclave.

clue.text: A place of purgatory and pointless summer fashion accessories

indicators.note: pointless removes a compass point, here south, from the sunglasses

parts.note: shades are sunglasses

explanation.surface: A grumble that summer accessories are torture and serve no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless looks like useless; it means losing a compass point (N, S, E or W).
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek underworld, a gloomy realm of the dead, loosely a place of suffering.

clue.text: The nation's back in the grip of top right-wing alliance

indicators.note: in the grip of means held tightly, so the reversed nation sits inside the top

parts.note: a lid is the top of a container

indicators.note: back here means the nation's letters are read in the backward direction

parts.note: the UK is the nation the magazine writes for

explanation.surface: Britain is being dragged back into the clutches of a powerful right-wing coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after nation stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Likud is the Israeli political party formed in 1973 as a coalition of right-wing groups.

clue.text: Stiff, right inside … shrunk

indicators.note: inside places the letter for right within the word for stiff

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, so stiff here means dead

explanation.surface: Something stiff, and then something shrunk: a bawdy before-and-after with an ellipsis for the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads stiff as an erection; in the wordplay a stiff is a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: Decreased and shrunk both mean having grown smaller in size or amount.

clue.text: Snotty hack (news agency) is after bribe

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
a hack is a journalist, and the ED is the editor who commands them
UP is United Press, the American news agency

explanation.surface: A sneering journalist from a wire service is on the take.
explanation.walkthrough: Snotty looks like it means arrogant; here it means full of snot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose that is bunged up is blocked with mucus, which is literally snotty.

clue.text: Rank, crappy products in South America

indicators.note: in places the shoddy goods inside south plus America

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: A complaint that cheap, rubbishy goods are sold across South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank looks like an adjective meaning foul, matching crappy; it is the noun meaning standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's position or standing in a hierarchy, the same as one's rank.

clue.text: The president's possibly not beneath being a scrubber

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue puts the rearranged word below, so after, the scrubbing

parts.note: a scrubber cleans, so being one is washing

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of not may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The president, maybe, is not above working as a cleaner, or a woman of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubber is also British slang for a promiscuous woman, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first president of the United States.

clue.text: Woman feasted topless, going on about Fanny

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the word for feasted

parts.note: to have feasted is to have eaten

indicators.note: about turns the word for Fanny round

parts.note: fanny is American slang for the bottom, as is ass

explanation.surface: A woman dined bare-breasted and wouldn't stop talking about someone called Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny is a name in the surface; in American slang it means backside, though in British slang it is ruder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a woman's first name, a short form of Theresa.

clue.text: Cook's range: large number wild topless women to northern Greek hero

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of cooking range
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: wild says the remaining letters run riot and are rearranged
topless takes the first letter off women

parts.note: only its last four letters are used

explanation.surface: A cook's sprawling range takes in hordes of wild bare-breasted women alongside a northern Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king who led the Greeks in the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Abominable Snowman's first two balls Thelma jiggled

indicators.note: jiggled means shaken about, so all these letters are mixed together
first, after Snowman's, takes just the opening letter of that word

parts.note: only its first letter is used
two balls are two round letter Os
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Yeti's testicles get a jiggle from someone called Thelma.
explanation.walkthrough: Abominable Snowman looks like one phrase, but Abominable is the definition and Snowman starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Abominable and loathsome both describe something that causes intense disgust or hatred.

clue.text: To go in for sex is something that inflames and makes you extremely loose

definitions.text: something that inflames and makes you extremely loose

parts.note: to enter is to go in
it is a coy word for sex
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude observation that sex leaves you sore and very slack.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose here means loose in the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, which typically causes diarrhoea.

clue.text: Ms Hurley a flutter in the embrace of — wouldn't you say? — our Brenda

indicators.note: in the embrace of means held inside the interjection

parts.note: eh is the tag asking for agreement
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen; the familiar short form of her first name is used
a flutter is a small bet

explanation.surface: Elizabeth Hurley has a gamble and ends up hugging the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called the Queen Brenda, so our Brenda stands for her first name in familiar form.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Hurley is the English actress and model, so her first name is the answer.

clue.text: Short length TV series: Having it off with a sloth

parts.note: in. is the short form of inch, a length
ER is the American hospital drama series

indicators.note: off means going wrong, so it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV listing: a short series about someone having sex with a lazy tree mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is laziness or reluctance to move or act, the deadly sin of sloth.

clue.text: Tiny demands snog and sex

parts.note: snog is British slang for kiss and cuddle, the same as to pet
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A small person insists on kissing and sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit is French for small, and appears in English phrases such as petit four for something little.

clue.text: Vat fiddle by Brenda, an arse-over-tip boozer

indicators.note: fiddle suggests tampering, so the letters of vat are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose royal cipher is ER

indicators.note: arse-over-tip means head over heels, so an is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Queen fiddles her VAT return and turns out to be a drunk who keeps falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax; arse over tip is British slang for falling head over heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a Greek tavern or restaurant, and boozer is British slang for a pub.

clue.text: Copper in Home Counties got married and was sick

indicators.note: in places the coin's letter inside the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the SE of England
P stands for penny, a copper coin
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: A policeman from the commuter belt round London marries and then throws up.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman; it is a copper coin, the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, so spewed means vomited, or was sick.

clue.text: See 1
Having an easy time briefly taking in sex partner

parts.note: inc. is the short form of including, which means taking in
a lover is a sexual partner

explanation.surface: Someone has it easy for a short while because they have taken a lover into their home.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in clover is an idiom for living in comfort and ease, like cattle in a rich pasture.

clue.text: Apply pressure to member, toss extremely briskly

parts.note: to lob is to toss something high

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of briskly

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Instructions for squeezing a male organ and masturbating quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Member looks anatomical; it is a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to try to influence legislators, putting pressure on members of parliament.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval on Monday for Blair we hear

definitions.note: said aloud, Blair sounds like blare, a loud noise; a boom is a deep loud noise, so the definition is the soundalike word

parts.note: boo is the noise a crowd makes to show disapproval

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, newly re-elected, gets booed at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by sound: Blair is pronounced like blare. The surface wants the prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a loud, harsh sound, and a boom is a deep, resonant loud sound, so they are near-synonyms.

clue.text: Absolutely and repeatedly expose homosexuals

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal publicly that they are gay
taken as written
repeatedly says the word for exposing is given a second time

explanation.surface: A campaigner insists they are completely committed to outing gay people over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means thorough or complete, so it works as a stand-in for absolute.

clue.text: Monarch nestling between tits, fly open

indicators.note: nestling between puts the monarch's letter in the middle of the word for tits

parts.note: a bust is a woman's breasts
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A king snuggled into a cleavage, with his trouser fly undone.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly open reads as an unbuttoned trouser fly; it is a verb phrase meaning to break open suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break or fly apart suddenly from pressure inside.

clue.text: Mark 11 …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pen name of the American author pairs this surname with the first name Mark
second meaning: read as the Roman numeral II, two, for which the archaic word is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The 11 is the Roman numeral II, two: an archaic word for two follows Mark to give the author of Huckleberry Finn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American writer Samuel Clemens; twain is an old word for two.

clue.text: … millionaire, being ready, pants

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash, money
bags is old British slang for loose trousers, which Americans call pants

explanation.surface: Following on from Mark: a rich man, prepared and wearing trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is an informal nickname for a very wealthy person.
